name: Seagull Party.aif
description:
Recorded with a Zoom H2n  on Crosby Beach in Liverpool  on 29/08/2020 the wind was approx 15mph.


This recording is a lot cleaner than the others, I've moved location to a quieter space away from the water and a bit more protection from the wind (I did have a wind breaker on the mic as well as Rycote suspension on the tripod.  So it's a fairly clear recording of the seagulls. There's also a dog barking in the distance free of charge.    I have still used the Izotope noise reduction on this, so again if anyone would like a copy of the unedited raw audio just drop me a message.  

Hope this useful for you guys. 

Chris :)

name: Sea, Rocks, Shoreline, Water, Crickets and Seaguls in front of the Ionian Sea at Early Morning
description:
Field recording captured at sunrise on the Ionian coast in Puglia, Italy. Gentle waves roll onto the rocky shoreline while crickets continue their dawn chorus and seagulls call overhead, creating a rich Mediterranean soundscape. This natural ambience captures the peaceful transition from night to morning and is ideal for documentaries, film, relaxation, meditation, and environmental sound design.

Recorded with a Zoom H1essential.

name: Seagulls, Ducks and Carp Fish Feeding Frenzy - Lake Mead, Nevada USA
description:
This is the sound of seagulls, ducks and other water birds competing with gigantic carp fish, and each other, for food on Lake Mead. It starts mellow and and grows into a full-blown frenzy with lots of calling, quacking, chirping, splashing, thrashing and slurping (from the fish).

The Hoover Dam isn't far from this lake, so tourist helicopters occasionally pass by. I hope you all like it. :)

name: Henne beach waves and seagulls 2013-02-09.wav
description: I went for a walk at one of the local beaches and decided to record a little. There was almost no wind at all, but some waves still. After walking for about half an hour, i found a perfect spot, right beside a lot of seagulls and their nestlings. Slowly and quietly i placed my recorder, without scaring the birds away. And after walking away, i could see the birds running around the mic. Around two minutes (plus minus) into the recording, you can actually hear the small and quick steps all around. The rest is all about waves, and hearing the big seagulls. Enjoy! Recorded with a zoom h2. You can find a picture here: http://www.flickr.com/photos/pkslot/8458334668/in/photostream
